MorphoHand · real_v1 hand D6 on the working plant · finger-only reorientation of the screwdriver, PPO in MuJoCo-Warp · 8–9 October 2026 · built 2026-10-09 13:13

Performance, consistency and transfer of reorientation policies trained with four fingertip contact models

Replayed open loop in CPU MuJoCo, Drake and Newton, the finger targets of the policies trained on the 1 mm sphere pads and on the pads mounted on a sprung skin kept the screwdriver in 167 of 170 replays, and those trained with MuJoCo point contact on the box tip or the TPU block mesh in 3 of 114. Closed loop in MuJoCo-Warp under the other contact models of the TPU block, the skin policies held 99 % of the rollouts, the pad policies 76 % and the TPU-mesh policies 51 % (89 % and 12 % for its two seeds).

The stopping rule of the checkpoint watch (every watched checkpoint degenerate for 10 M steps) stops all three box-tip seeds and two of three TPU-mesh seeds at 16 M steps for dropping every rollout, shaking the tool or rocking the tool at every policy step, and one of three pad seeds and one of three skin seeds at 16 and 24 M steps for rocking the tool at every policy step or shaking the tool (three of these runs in hindsight: they were watched after training to 40 M steps, and their final policies are kept). In the hold of the final policies the tool’s shaking is 35–302 rad/s² with point contact and 9–26 rad/s² with the pads and the skin (trajectory_health fails a policy above 40). The point-contact policies turn further where they hold: final held cosine 0.94 for the box tip (36/64 rollouts held) and 0.84–0.86 for the TPU mesh, against 0.61–0.69 for the pads and 0.62–0.79 for the skin, all of whose rollouts held (320/320). On an idle GPU a training iteration costs 1.7× the TPU mesh’s time with the pads and 2.3× with the skin.

Terms and metrics

arm
One fingertip contact model the policies train on. All arms share the hand (real_v1 D6), the working plant (finger servo kp 4 N m/rad, damping 0.08 N m s/rad, torque limit 1 N m), the tool (the 24.5 g screwdriver, = 1), the solver (MuJoCo-Warp, 2 ms, 10 Newton iterations, elliptic cones, impratio 10), the recipe and its flags, and differ only in the fingertip.
env step, iteration
One env step is one 20 ms policy step of one of the 2,048 parallel envs; one PPO iteration collects 24 steps per env, 49,152 env steps. 40 M env steps are 813 iterations.
held (load test)
At a policy step, at least two fingertips each press on the tool with at least 0.24 N (its weight) and the tool is above 60 mm. A rollout is held when this is true at its last step (5 s).
cos
The signed cosine of the tool’s own axis with world vertical, ; +1 is tip down, the goal of the turn; the tool starts horizontal (cos 0).
held cosine
The mean of the final cos over the held rollouts of one evaluation. The turn the policy achieved, counted only where the hand still carries the tool.
evaluation
64 rollouts of the deterministic policy (its mean action) in parallel envs for 250 policy steps, with the training’s timing (residual and reorientation reward from step 58, after the scripted grasp and lift), no early termination and no randomisation; 256 per cell of the transfer matrix and 128 per perturbation. The rollouts differ only through the GPU contact solve.
reach 0.9, step at 0.9
Rollouts whose tool passes cos 0.9 at a step at which it is held, whether or not it is still held at 5 s; the median policy step at which it first does.
seed spread
Range of the held cosines (or held fractions) of one arm’s seeds that trained to 40 M steps.
rollout spread
Standard deviation of the final cos over the held rollouts of one evaluation, averaged over seeds.
grip
Sum of the three fingertips’ net contact force on the tool, mean over the held steps from step 58, N.
|Δa|
Mean absolute change of the 9-dimensional action between consecutive policy steps, in action units (one unit is 0.5 rad of servo target); 0 for a policy that holds still.
contacts per step
Fingertip-tool contacts summed over the three tips (the fingertip sensor’s match count), mean over the held steps.
penetration
Deepest fingertip-tool penetration over a rollout’s held steps, mm; mean over held rollouts.
creep
Displacement of the tool against the palm over the last second of the rollout divided by 0.98 s (mm/s), and the rotation of its axis over the same second (°/s); median over held rollouts.
peak force
Largest single-fingertip net force over a rollout’s held steps, N; mean over held rollouts.
transfer gap
Held fraction (or held cosine) under another contact model or simulator minus that under the policy’s own contact model in MuJoCo-Warp.
shaking
Mean absolute change of the tool’s angular speed between consecutive policy steps, divided by the 20 ms step, over the held steps of the hold after the turn (policy steps 150–250), rad/s²; median over held rollouts. trajectory_health fails a policy for jitter above 40 rad/s²; the still pad and skin holds of the final policies read 9–18 rad/s².
checkpoint watch
At every 82nd iteration (4.0 M env steps) the training run is paused, the checkpoint evaluated (64 rollouts) and its median and worst rollouts rendered as frame strips and a film, which are looked at before the run continues; the owner’s rule stops a run that is degenerate for 10 M steps (drops every rollout, an idle finger, jitter, saturated actions, or the tool on the palm) or whose held cosine gains under 0.02 over 10 M steps. Jitter counts when the shaking exceeds 40 rad/s² while the rocking exceeds 0.005, and rocking above 0.005 counts on its own when the tilting velocity reverses at most steps; the strips and the consecutive-step frames of the hold were looked at for every checkpoint. The seed-0 runs and the skin runs were watched on the same checkpoints after training.
servo targets at a limit
Share of the nine finger servo targets (anchor plus residual) at their actuator’s range limit over the active steps; the residual itself is not clipped in these runs.
finger share
One fingertip’s share of the summed fingertip-tool force over the held steps.
rocking
Median absolute change of the tool’s cos between consecutive policy steps over the held steps of the hold (steps 150–250). Above 0.005 with the tilting velocity reversing at most steps, the tool rocks at the policy rate, an oscillation the shaking misses because the angular speed keeps its magnitude.
grip change per step
Median absolute change of the summed fingertip-tool force between consecutive policy steps over the held steps of the hold (steps 150–250), N; a steady grip reads near 0.
open-loop replay
From the state at policy step 58 of a MuJoCo-Warp rollout, the policy’s recorded finger targets are played into another simulator at 50 Hz with the palm welded at its lifted pose (scripts/rl_policy_replay.py); the policy does not see that simulator’s state.

Contact models and training cost

All arms train the same hand, plant, tool, solver, recipe and flags and differ only in the fingertip. The box tip is the fingertip every policy of this program trained on until 2026-10-05. The TPU arms replace it by the printed tip, a 17×14.8×22 mm block with 2.7 mm fillets, as one convex mesh with point contact, or as the 1 mm sphere pads of the overview page (docs/experiments/20261009-contact_overview/20261009-sphere_pad_contact_model.html). The skin mounts each tip’s pads on a child body with two tangent slides and a hinge about the palmar normal, sprung by Mindlin’s and Lubkin’s initial stiffness and on the pads’ patch at 12 N ( = 3.66 mm, 65 kN/m, 0.90 N m/rad) and critically damped; it is the presliding candidate kept on the native-compliance page (docs/experiments/20261007-native_compliance/20261007-native_presliding_compliance.html). On the hand it runs at the env’s impratio 10 (1000 diverges under ten solver iterations) with the slide armature set to . Condim 4, a point contact whose spin torque is bounded by with = 3.0 mm (the pads’ twist-onset arm at 10–20 N, twist_onset/tip_T2.jsonl), is evaluated in the transfer matrix but not trained. Training used 18.6 of the 24 GPU-hours budgeted.

Films of the final policies

Transfer to other contact models and simulators

Closed loop in MuJoCo-Warp under the other contact models of the TPU block, the skin policies held 2,283 of 2,304 rollouts (99 %), the pad policies 1,173 of 1,536 (76 %) and the TPU-mesh policies 782 of 1,536 (51 %: seed 1 held 686, seed 0 96). The box-tip policy held 26 of 1,024 (3 %) on the TPU block, and on the box tip, a different shape, only the skin policies held more than a quarter of the rollouts (442 of 768). Open-loop replays held, per contact model the policy trained on: box: CPU MuJoCo 0/16, Drake 0/16, Newton 0/6; TPU mesh: CPU MuJoCo 0/32, Drake 3/32, Newton 0/12; pads: CPU MuJoCo 32/32, Drake 32/32, Newton 10/12; skin: CPU MuJoCo 37/38, Drake 38/38, Newton 18/18. CPU MuJoCo steps each policy’s own fingertip model, so for the point-contact policies only the implementation changes, and their tool falls a median 0.32 s after the onset there (0.68 s in Drake, 0.52 s in Newton). The pad and skin replays end within a median 0.002 of the MuJoCo-Warp rollout’s final cosine in CPU MuJoCo (−0.077 to +0.057), a median 0.05 below it in Drake and 0.09 below it in Newton.

Learning curves and the checkpoint watch

The checkpoint at which a run first held at least 60 of 64 rollouts: box s0 not by 40 M, s1 8 M, s2 not by 16 M; TPU mesh s0 16 M, s1 4 M, s2 8 M; pads s0 12 M, s1 4 M, s2 4 M; skin s0 8 M, s1 4 M, s2 8 M. An episode ends 15 steps after a fingertip leaves the tool, so a policy that drops the tool collects the return of about 75 steps (Figure 7); the box tip’s seed 0 stayed there for 28 M steps.

The policies trained on the pads and the skin end training with an action noise of 0.10–0.15, the TPU-mesh policies with 0.17 and the box-tip policy with 0.30; every run starts at 0.30.

The owner’s stopping rule applied at every watched checkpoint (4.0 M steps apart): stop when every checkpoint of the last 10 M steps is degenerate (a flag of the checkpoint watch), or when the held cosine gained under 0.02 (and the held count under 8 of 64) over 10 M steps. The seed-0 runs finished before the watch existed, and the skin trainer leaves too little GPU memory for a second process: those runs were watched after they ended.

Final policies

Every final policy brings the tool to 90 % of its final cosine within 0.34 s of the onset and then holds it (Figure 14). The grip in that hold separates the contact models: the summed fingertip force spans (10th–90th percentile over the held steps, per seed) box 41–148; TPU mesh 38–62, 44–67; pads 42–44, 52–57; skin 46–52, 46–49, 48–55 N.

Perturbations of the plant, the tool and the grasp

The servo gain is the perturbation that separates the policies. At = 10 N m/rad, 2.5× the training plant’s, the policies lose the tool after the onset (median loss at policy step 72–219) in all but skin seed 2 (99 of 128 held); at 6 N m/rad the point-contact policies held 209 of 384 rollouts and the pad and skin policies 527 of 640. Friction ±30 %, tool mass ±20 %, the 1 ms step and the grasp-pose noise keep every TPU-block policy at 95 % held or more except pads seed 0 at the pose noise (119 of 128) and skin seed 0 at friction ×0.7 (100 of 128); the box-tip policy holds 66–84 of 128 under these and at the nominal. At 2 N m/rad TPU mesh seed 0 turns the tool to 0.69 instead of 0.86 and pads seed 0 turns the tool to 0.05 instead of 0.69.

What this does not settle

  • Bench replay of the finger targets. The replays test the policies in three simulators and none of them is the printed fingertip. The next measurement plays the recorded finger targets of the median rollout of the pads, skin and TPU-mesh final policies on the hand at 50 Hz from the lifted grasp (a plan exported from logs/20261008-contact_model_policies/replay/<tag>/rec.npz through the real_v1 deploy format, 10 trials each, tracked). The result that contradicts this page: the TPU-mesh targets hold the tool as often as the pad or skin targets.
  • Grip force. The recipe copied from the 2026-09-17 60 M run gives the grip term a weight of +0.25, a small bonus above 4 N per pad, and every final policy grips with 40–100 N on a 24.5 g tool. Fine-tune the pads and skin finals with weight −5 (the 2026-09-17 finetune setting) and repeat the replays; the comparison holds if the replays still keep the tool at a grip near 10 N.
  • Unclipped residual. The runs train without an action clip: actions reach 3 units (1.5 rad past the anchor) and one pip servo target per compliant policy sits at its extension limit in 95 % of the steps (Table 4). A deployable residual needs clip_actions 1.0 (src/morphohand/rl/ppo_config.py); retrain one seed per compliant arm with it and compare the held cosine.
  • Servo gain. Every final policy but skin seed 2 loses the tool at = 10 N m/rad, the top of the 2026-10-06 readback range, and the runs train at 4. Fine-tune the pad and skin finals with drawn per episode from 2–10 (a reset event in _build_events of src/morphohand/rl/env_build.py, which has none yet) and repeat scripts/rl_contact_eval.py robust --perturb kp=2 kp=6 kp=10; a fine-tuned policy that still loses the tool at 10 would mean the turn depends on the soft servo.
  • Seeds of the point-contact arms. The stop rule leaves one box-tip seed, two TPU-mesh seeds, two pad seeds and three skin seeds with a final policy; the point-contact seed spread rests on those runs, and the box tip’s only finished seed meets the rule in hindsight. Two more box-tip and TPU-mesh seeds trained to 40 M without the rule (about 1.3 GPU-h each) show whether a point-contact policy that keeps the tool still exists; one that holds 64/64 with a shaking under 40 rad/s² and survives the CPU MuJoCo replay would contradict the finding that point-contact training shakes the tool loose.
